title: Lollapalooza Shortens Wolf Alice and Cortis Sets, Delays Several More Amid Intense Flooding
description: Day three of Lollapalooza has been delayed from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. CT. Most of the sets scheduled within that three-hour window have been canceled, w
body:
Day three of Lollapalooza has been delayed from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. CT. Most of the sets scheduled within that three-hour window have been canceled, with a few exceptions. K-pop group Cortis, who have been moved to later this afternoon, will be performing for 40 minutes rather than their previously scheduled 50. English band Wolf Alice, originally scheduled to take the Bud Light stage at 3 p.m., has been pushed to 4 p.m., with their hour-long set slashed to just 30 minutes.
	

	The delay comes following heavy rainfall overnight in Chicago. The poor weather is forecast to continue throughout the day and has led to localized flooding. Early this morning, photos of a swamp-like Hutchinson Field, home to both the T-Mobile and Allianz stages, began circulating on social media, and by 9:30 a.m. CT, Lollapalooza released an official statement across their social media platforms, saying, “Due to current and overnight heavy rains, doors will be delayed until 2 p.m. Please continue to watch this space for further updates.”


	Just under three hours later, a second statement was put out, reading: “Thank you for your patience. At this time, we are actively working on cleaning up areas of the grounds with an updated plan to open doors at 3 p.m, with the Box Office opening at 1 p.m. Please continue to watch this space for further updates.”

	The updated schedule came at 1:30 p.m. CT, an hour and a half ahead of doors. Today’s headliners are Olivia Dean and Jennie. Neither set time was affected by the rain delay. Other anticipated sets include The Neighbourhood, Geese, Sienna Spiro, Clipse and Ethel Cain.
	

Your updated Saturday schedule is here! Grant Park will be muddy, so come prepared. Wear waterproof shoes you don't mind getting wet and muddy, be patient as you make your way around the grounds, and most importantly – bring all the positive vibes. See you soon! pic.twitter.com/5oKRlSPCI5— Lollapalooza (@lollapalooza) August 1, 2026


	At this time, Sunday’s schedule, which marks the festival’s fourth and final day, will continue as planned. Fans can expect performances from headliners Tate McRae and The XX, alongside other standout acts Adéla, Jade, Aespa and Stella Lefty.

schema.headline: Lollapalooza Shortens Wolf Alice and Cortis Sets, Delays Several More Amid Intense Flooding

title: ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary
description: “Wild Inside” is an enchanting movie, and a haunting one too. It’s a documentary about Flaco, the owl who escaped from the Central Park Zoo and spen
body:
“Wild Inside” is an enchanting movie, and a haunting one too. It’s a documentary about Flaco, the owl who escaped from the Central Park Zoo and spent a year living in the wilds of New York City. Since that story was widely covered when it happened in 2023, turning Flaco into an international media sensation, you might think: Why do I need to see a documentary about it?

	The answer is that Penny Lane, the gifted director of “Wild Inside,” has told this tale in a revelatory way, building it like an imagistic storybook from the ground up. From the moment that Flaco, on the evening of February 2, 2023, first appeared on a sidewalk near the corner of 50th St. and Fifth Avenue, standing there as still as a statue, he was surrounded by people filming and photographing him — civilians on their phones, then nature photographers, amateur and professional. Working with the editor Hannah Buck, Lane uses their endless archive of images to craft a true-life nature fairy tale. “Wild Inside” feels like the vérité version of the greatest children’s novel E.B. White never wrote.
	

	As you watch the movie, Flaco becomes a true character, though there’s nothing cute about him, and the film has a philosophical ambiguity that takes you by surprise. It’s a movie about freedom and captivity, but it doesn’t have a simple or reductive message. Flaco, who lived in the Central Park Zoo for 13 years, escaped when someone cut the wire mesh on his cage. He was a Eurasian eagle owl, a species that doesn’t exist in America, and when you look at him, he really is the living incarnation of the classic, mythological…owl. He’s stunningly beautiful, with big orange eyes set inside a regal head, and a body of tan and black and orange feathers that makes it appear that he’s wrapped inside the most luxurious comforter on earth. His wingspan is awesome (nearly six feet wide), but when Flaco is just standing there, which is most of the time, he does indeed look wise and inscrutable. To know what’s going on in that head, you have to read his actions.
	

	The day after he made his first appearance on that midtown sidewalk, Flaco flew to Central Park and lodged himself high up in a tree near the south end of the park, just opposite the Essex House. What would happen to him? Representatives of the Central Park Zoo planned to recapture him, and they set about the task armed with mosquito nets, trying to tempt Flaco with food — the dead white lab rats he had eaten every day for 13 years. But Flaco wasn’t interested. He just stayed up in that tree. How would he survive?  Tentatively, then with more confidence, he began to fly down into the park and hunt the real live New York City rats that roam there. His muscles grew stronger; his predatory instincts came to the fore. Within two weeks, he was living like a wild animal, though one who was so accustomed to being around humans that he had a way of standing on a branch as if it were his throne. The Central Park Zoo people gave up on trying to capture him.

	It’s only natural that the story told by “Wild Inside” triggers our liberal impulses. We think: Yes! Flaco is alive in the wild! He’s in a better place. The movie taps into what’s noble and valid and genuine about those feelings. Some of us actually have an aversion to zoos. Personally speaking, from the earliest age, I couldn’t stand them. I found staring at wild animals in captivity to be inexpressibly sad. Flaco is the animal hero who triumphs over the system of “benign” incarceration, becoming the apex predator of Central Park. And the more he thrives, and gets elevated to a kind of critter superhero status (Seth Meyers on his late-night show: “Every New Yorker dreams of moving out of their tiny shitty apartment into a nicer neighborhood. And Flaco Shawshanked out of that cage and did it!”), the more he becomes a symbol of what freedom means. After a number of months, he moves from Central Park to the East Village, and then to the Upper West Side, where we see him standing on air conditioners, and at times on elevated stone carvings in a way that’s very Batman. Residents will encounter him perched on the air conditioner just outside their apartment, staring in.

	From the outset, however, there are warnings in the other direction. Within a week, Flaco had triumphed over the doubters who feared that an owl raised in captivity wouldn’t have the strength or stamina to survive in the outside world. Yet it isn’t quite that simple. There have long been owls and hawks who live outside of zoos in New York, and there’s a fate that awaits them. They eat rats and mice, and in doing so they absorb the rodenticide that’s in the bodies of those creatures.
	

	Should Flaco have been recaptured and returned to his tiny environment within the Central Park Zoo? In the documentary, several knowledgable observers say that that would have been the most humane scenario — that had it happened that way, Flaco would be alive today, and would likely have lived for another 30 to 40 years. The probability of that is indisputable. What’s haunting about “Wild Inside” is that it inspires us to root for Flaco’s freedom, for the fullness of his life, in the spirit of “It’s better to burn out than to fade away.” Yet the ending that he comes to haunts us as well. He dies one day, out of the blue, by colliding into the wall of an apartment courtyard; that’s because his strength had been weakened by the rodenticide. What was the right choice? Maybe there was no right choice. “Wild Inside” is so moving because we’re stirred by the creature Flaco was, and it’s the story he lived that made him that creature.

schema.headline: ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary

title: Richard L. O’Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer and ‘The Muppet Movie’ Executive, Dies at 96
description: Richard L. O’Connor, an Emmy-winning producer known for his work as an executive in charge of productions like “The Muppet Movie,” “On Golden Pond”
body:
Richard L. O’Connor, an Emmy-winning producer known for his work as an executive in charge of productions like “The Muppet Movie,” “On Golden Pond” and “Hickey & Boggs,” died July 22 in Palm Desert, California. He was 96.

	O’Connor’s death was confirmed to Variety by his family.

	O’Connor won an Emmy back in 1990 for his work on “A Mother’s Courage: The Mary Thomas Story.” He also received nominations for producing “The Final Days,” a chronicle of Richard Nixon’s last months in the White House, and “Fatal Vision,” a miniseries starring Eva Marie Saint, Karl Malden and Barry Newman.
	

	As an executive in charge of production, O’Connor’s credits include “Across 110th Street,” “Raise the Titanic,” “Borderline,” “Hard Country” and “Barbarosa,” along with multiple TV movies like “Sanctuary of Fear,” “Friendly Fire” and an adaptation of “All Quiet on the Western Front.”


	His work as a producer spanned across the ’70s into the 2000s, with credits on “Run, Joe, Run,” “NBC Special Treat,” “Shades of LA,” “Children of the Dark” and “Voices from the Grave.” On his last project, 2001’s “Face Value,” he was credited as co-executive producer.

	O’Connor retired after multiple decades in the business and lived out his years near San Francisco’s Botanical Gardens. He was born in San Francisco on Jan. 7, 1930. Along with his twin brother, Don, he served in the U.S. Marine Corps during the Korean War. O’Connor eventually moved to Los Angeles, getting his start at CBS Television City in the mailroom.

	O’Connor is survived by daughters Kathleen, Triglia and Karen, stepchildren Kate, Marc and Matt, and grandchildren Rachael, Kayleigh, Seth and Joshua.

schema.headline: Richard L. O’Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer and ‘The Muppet Movie’ Executive, Dies at 96

title: Juliette Lewis on Fiery ‘Cape Fear’ Finale, ‘Nostalgic’ Nods to 1991 Film and Why Crystal Will ‘Haunt’ Max Forever
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for “The Executioners,” the finale of “Cape Fear,” now streaming on Apple TV.

	Nothing good ever happens
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for “The Executioners,” the finale of “Cape Fear,” now streaming on Apple TV.

	Nothing good ever happens on a houseboat in a “Cape Fear” adaptation — just ask Juliette Lewis.

	In Martin Scorsese’s 1991 version — for which she was nominated for an Oscar at 18 years old — Lewis’ character Danielle was seduced, assaulted and terrorized on her family’s houseboat by Max Cady (Robert De Niro), a serial rapist who used her as a naive pawn to get revenge on her father (Nick Nolte), the lawyer who’d put him away. She survived that boat ride, but washes up on the banks of the titular North Carolina river with bumps, bruises, a bit of whiplash and a complete loss of her innocence. 
	

	Lewis, on the other hand, had a blast.


	“That was so fun, which is probably weird to say, but it was because I was with Jessica Lange and De Niro, and they’re doing push-ups between scenes,” Lewis tells Variety. “We all did jumping jacks to get our heart rate up to play that terror. That’s where I cut my teeth, and I learned the tricks of the trade. I take what I learned from that movie, and it’s fed me my whole career.”

	Those lessons have particularly resonated this summer when she joined Apple TV and creator Nick Antosca’s series adaptation of “Cape Fear,” in which she plays something wholly different: Crystal, the show’s villain, and a vicious one at that. But in the opening scene of this week’s finale, she still ends up on yet another houseboat — and this time she isn’t so lucky. 
	

	Since she was first introduced as the masked-and-hooded mystery woman stalking Max (Javier Bardem), Crystal has been an unpredictable element in his otherwise calculated and manipulative plot for revenge against Anna (Amy Adams) and Tom Bowden (Patrick Wilson), the lawyers who got him convicted after they fell in love as opposing counsel. But as Anna learned in last week’s penultimate episode, Crystal is actually Max’s sister, and she was particularly cruel toward him in their youth before they seemingly shared a sexual relationship, which Anna believes resulted in a child. These grim discoveries came out of a brief buddy-cop partnership between Anna and Crystal.

	“It was fun to play two people that kind of are enjoying each other’s company, or are they?” she says. “They’re both out to get something. They both know Crystal’s hiding something. It was fun having that dance with her, because I just admire Amy so much.”

	But ultimately, Crystal can’t let Anna go because she’s been working with Max all along. Crystal can’t quite control her family dysfunction either, and when Anna reveals to Crystal’s son Luke (Max Mattern) that he might be Uncle Max’s spawn, it ignites a screaming match between them that gives cover to Anna to slip into the river and swim away — but not before Crystal stabs her through the hand. When Max arrives at Crystal’s houseboat, he proves that Crystal was nothing more than a tool that is no longer useful to him. She pleads with him that she may have been horrible to him as a kid, but so was he to her. “We’re even now, right?” she begs of him, before he puts a bullet in her stomach and one in Luke’s as well.

	“In that scene with Javier, where our faces are so close, at one point the director wanted me to look in the camera,” Lewis says. “But I thought it was close enough. I like to keep some rules of cinema, and I like the way I am just looking at him. It was really special.”

	Lewis has had the rare pleasure of locking horns with two Max Cadys, first De Niro and now Bardem. She says she felt the gravity of that moment on both occasions.

	“They’re two greats of American cinema, and I very much felt that,” she says. “When I was working with Javier, oh my gosh, he’s fully consumed by the thing he is playing, and I just love it. It’s really something to witness, especially on the boat.”
	

	Speaking of the houseboat, the finale treads some familiar ground for Lewis. In the film, De Niro puts Lewis’ character in the hold of the boat and she later sets him on fire. In the finale, after shooting Crystal and Luke, Max throws them both in the hold and sets the boat on fire, with their father (Ron Perlman) left to burn in a cage on the deck. Lewis recognizes the parallels, and commends Antosca’s clever nods. But she’s still wrapping her head around reliving the “Cape Fear” houseboat experience for a second time.

	“I still do the push-ups and jumping jacks when I’m about to play a fearful scene, and that is because I saw Jessica and De Niro doing that,” she says. “You know, doing the series, it was a bit nostalgic to be on the houseboat again and playing a different person. But with all these high stakes, she fights. Ultimately, Crystal has to be a powerhouse of a villain for Max Cady. Nick knew that to bring me back, it can’t just be a little wink. It had to be something impactful.”

	The loose grip Crystal has on her sanity is what first drew Lewis back to the “Cape Fear” IP, continuing a tradition started by Gregory Peck and Robert Mitchum, the stars of the 1962 original who appeared in small roles in the 1991 version. (The two movies and now the Apple series were birthed from John D. MacDonald’s 1957 novel “The Executioners.”)

	“I really wanted to play a fractured personality, and that’s the ingredients that Nick wrote for me,” she says. “This is somebody who’s been going in and out of institutions. That’s sort of the energy we’re bringing. This is someone who vacillates between different ways of being. You could call it personalities, you could call it energy, but she lives in extremes.”

	Antosca gave Lewis a three-page backstory for Crystal, only some of which made it on screen. For that reason alone, she wants Crystal to survive the blaze on the houseboat, and it wouldn’t be a stretch. No charred bodies are given as proof by the end of the episode –– and the Bowdens ultimately spare Max’s life.

	“And we were surrounded by water!” Lewis says, suggesting possible escape routes.

	Regardless of whether it was indeed a watery grave for Crystal, Lewis holds onto one simple truth: “She’s going to haunt him till the end of time,” she says.

schema.headline: Juliette Lewis on Fiery ‘Cape Fear’ Finale, ‘Nostalgic’ Nods to 1991 Film and Why Crystal Will ‘Haunt’ Max Forever

title: The Rolling Stones ‘Behind the Song’: See Mick Jagger and Producer Andrew Watt’s Deep Dive on the Creation of ‘Mr. Charm’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Unlike most of his peers, the lead singer of the world’s greatest rock and roll band has never been one for looking back, even at the recent past. T
body:
Unlike most of his peers, the lead singer of the world’s greatest rock and roll band has never been one for looking back, even at the recent past. There’s a scene in one of the countless Rolling Stones documentaries in which that singer — Mick Jagger — and drummer Charlie Watts are walking into Olympic Studios in London, the incubator of some of their greatest work, and rather than waxing nostalgic, Jagger exclaims, “Old recording sessions — who gives a shit?” before he gamely gets back on the task and shares some memories. 
	

	And although there are certainly some videos of him sitting in a studio listening to the band’s music and commenting on it, he has never before done a “Behind the Song”-style dissection and analysis of one of the band’s songs — until now.


	Variety captured Jagger and Andrew Watt, producer of the band’s two most recent albums, 2023’s “Hackney Diamonds” and the new “Foreign Tongues,” at London’s Metropolis Studios doing exactly that with “Mr. Charm,” a song from the latter collection. You won’t find it on any greatest-hits compilations (it was released less than a month ago), but it’s in the classic Rolling Stones mold, and this remarkable 15-minute video illuminates, in many ways as never before, the group’s creative process.



	Jagger and Watt take us through the creation of the song, from Jagger’s first demo — which began with a guitar riff and rough melody — which was then embellished and enhanced into what it is today. First Keith Richards added some chords that overtook Jagger’s originals as the song’s signature riff, then Ronnie Wood added some riffs of his own in response to Richards’, drummer Steve Jordan contributed the piledriving rhythm and percussion, and guest keyboardist Steve Winwood, who the Stones have known for sixty years, added some majestic B3 organ — and backing singer Naarai Jacobs joins Jagger on the chorus with some powerful wailing that recalls the classic “Gimme Shelter.” 
	

	(Incidentally, the interviewer — this writer — was the one to mention “Gimme Shelter,” which got a rather mocking response from Jagger. The reason for that reaction was illuminated later in the day at a press conference, where he said, “Journalists are always comparing your new work to what you’ve done before.”) 

	It’s an amazing breakdown of the Rolling Stones’ creative process, which obviously has evolved over the decades but remains the same in so many ways — and it is fascinating for deep Stones fans. 

	Jagger speaks of how counterintuitive it is that he, rather than Richards, is the one who likes punky, slashing guitar chords, as opposed to the more-refined approach of the band’s main guitarists.

	“I don’t think Ronnie and Keith really like me doing it,” he says, adding quickly with a laugh, “but I do it anyway!”

	Indeed, during one of the video’s most revealing clips, we hear Richards and Wood’s guitars in isolation, responding to each other like birds calling across a forest.

	Playing the guitar tracks in isolation, Watt says, “This is my favorite part,” he smiles as it plays. “You can’t overdub that — that’s [playing live] on the floor, looking at the person across from you, smiling, and playing off of each other.”

	“Doing my lick!” Jagger adds, and the two collapse into laughter.

	The two also elaborate on the embellishments added after the main track was recorded, including a “dirty-sounding, overdriven” acoustic guitar that Richards wanted to add. “ ‘I want to try a ‘Street Fighting Man’ kind of thing,’” Watt recalls him saying.



	

	



	Likewise, they recall Winwood bringing in a set of congas that longtime Stones producer Jimmy Miller gifted him — in fact, Miller first came onto the Stones radar thanks to his early work with Winwood in both the Spencer Davis Group and Traffic. As they play Jordan’s driving drums, embellished with maracas and the congas in question, Jagger talks about the imprtance of a song’s groove.

	“It’s connected with dance — the drums, the feet, and also the spitting out of the lyrics on a song like this, where you’ve got a lot of words coming at you very quickly and they’ve got to be in time.”

	In the video’s most hilarious moment, he also demonstrates — by grabbing and comically manipulating Watt’s arms — how on a very early Rolling Stones tour with Bo Diddley, the blues legend’s percussionist showed him how to play maracas properly.
	

	You’ll see all that and much more in Variety‘s “Behind the Song.”

schema.headline: The Rolling Stones ‘Behind the Song’: See Mick Jagger and Producer Andrew Watt’s Deep Dive on the Creation of ‘Mr. Charm’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Vin Diesel Says ‘Fast Forever’ Has the ‘Best Script I Have Read in Decades’: ‘I Am Still Crying’
description:
Vin Diesel has read the script for the 11th “Fast & Furious” film, and he is singing its praises.

	“I just read the ‘Fast Forever‘ script by [Micha
body:
Vin Diesel has read the script for the 11th “Fast & Furious” film, and he is singing its praises.

	“I just read the ‘Fast Forever‘ script by [Michael Lesslie]. It is the best script I have read in decades,” Diesel wrote on Instagram. “I am still crying…”

	The post was shared alongside a trailer for the upcoming re-release of the original “The Fast and the Furious” film, which is coming back to theaters on Aug. 21 in time for its 25th anniversary. That film starred Diesel alongside the late Paul Walker, Michelle Rodriguez, Jordana Brewster, Rick Yue and Chad Lindberg, kicking off the long-running action franchise after grossing $207 million worldwide (not adjusted for inflation).
	

	In his Instagram post, Diesel also teased that “Fast Forever” will have a tie to the original film: “You will thank God you got to see the First one in the theaters this summer.”


	“Fast Forever” is the latest film in the action franchise after “Fast X,” which was released in May 2023 and grossed $704 million worldwide. It left things off on a big cliffhanger, teasing Gal Gadot and Dwayne Johnson’s returns with two post-credit scenes. “Fast Forever” will be directed by Louis Leterrier, known for “The Transporter” and “The Incredible Hulk.”

	Lesslie was announced to be writing the script back in March. Sources told Variety that he rewrote a script previously penned by Aaron Rabin and Zach Dean. Lesslie has written “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” “Macbeth,” “Assassin’s Creed,” “Now You See Me: Now You Don’t” and “Hamlet” starring Riz Ahmed. He also penned the screenplay for “Sunrise on the Reaping,” which will hit  theaters on November 20, in addition to executive producing both “The Rescue” and “Thirteen Lives.”
	

	“Fast Forever” will release in theaters March 17, 2028.

schema.headline: Vin Diesel Says ‘Fast Forever’ Has the ‘Best Script I Have Read in Decades’: ‘I Am Still Crying’

title: ‘Barbie’ Sequel Stalls as David Zaslav Won’t Approve Bigger Salaries for Ryan Gosling and Margot Robbie
description: When a movie makes more than $1.4 billion at the box office and earns eight Academy Award nominations, the studio is going to want to make a sequel.
body:
When a movie makes more than $1.4 billion at the box office and earns eight Academy Award nominations, the studio is going to want to make a sequel. Such was the case with Warner Bros. and “Barbie.” But time is running out for the studio to put Margot Robbie back in pink.

	In a new report, The New York Times reveals that Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav has balked at giving Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling rich deals with profit participation for the second film. Gosling, who was nominated for a best supporting actor Oscar for his role as Ken, is angling to raise his pay to $20 million. A Warner Bros. spokesperson notes that there was never an agreed-upon framework that was approved and pulled back.
	

	In a rare move, Warner Bros. didn’t require the stars of “Barbie” to commit to sequels as they only signed a one-movie deal to land Greta Gerwig as the film’s director. (“Barbie” had experienced many false starts over the years until Gerwig provided her feminist take on the popular toy.)


	The Times report notes that Gerwig and her husband and “Barbie” writing partner Noah Baumbach have an idea for the new movie, but won’t share the concept with the studio until the deals are complete. Warner Bros. is on a mission to get its deals in place before the rights revert to Mattel in December. However, if the studio doesn’t come to terms with the “Barbie” crew by that deadline, Mattel would have to redevelop the IP for a new movie — meaning a new filmmaker, new cast and new concept.

	Warner Bros. co-chairs, Pam Abdy and Michael De Luca, confirmed the talks in a statement: “We have a rights deal with Mattel in place and have made a series of big offers to try and finalize deals to make the next ‘Barbie’ film. Unfortunately, we have been unable to reach an agreement thus far.”
	

	Over three years, the studio has made a half dozen offers to the creative team behind “Barbie.” The talent’s reps declined the most recent offer, which is among the biggest Warner Bros. has made for a film. No counter has been made to date.

	While it might seem like CAA — which represents Gerwig, Baumbach, Robbie and Gosling — is playing hardball, it’s standard practice to renegotiate contracts when a sequel wasn’t included in the original paperwork, as was the case for “Barbie.”

	The blockbuster movie, released in July 2023, catapulted filmmaker Gerwig, producer-star Robbie and Gosling to new heights and was a huge win for Mattel, which owns the rights to the fashion doll, too — especially as the toy brand aims to stake its claim in Hollywood.

	“It’s funny, that knee-jerk reaction in this day and age for everyone to immediately ask about a sequel,” Robbie told Variety for a 2024 cover story, heralding her production company LuckyChap as showpersons of the year. “I don’t think it was like that 20 years ago. This wasn’t designed to be a trilogy.”

	That said, all parties were open to the idea of more pink-hued adventures, but nothing could happen unless Gerwig and Baumbach came back with another great idea.

	“Everything went into ‘Barbie’ — and that’s how Greta works,” Robbie said at the time. “She finishes every movie on empty, feeling like she could never make another movie because she put everything she had into that one. So I don’t know what it would take to fill that cup up again for her. Or for us. I think Warners would also agree. I don’t know what more could even look like. We want to make more films that have the effect that ‘Barbie’ has.”

	In an interesting coincidence, the “Barbie 2” report comes as “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” breaks box office records, because there’s a universe where that movie never happened. Remember 2019, when Sony and Marvel’s agreement to co-finance and creatively produce Tom Holland’s “Spider-Man” movies; following public outcry (and tears of Holland’s own), the two parties came back to the negotiating table and hammered out a new deal. The resulting films, 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home,” stand as the franchise’s highest-grossing film, with $1.9 billion worldwide, and “Brand New Day” looks to reach or surpass those numbers. So, reaching an agreement on a “Barbie” sequel will likely prove lucrative for all parties involved. 
	

	While December is the deadline for a new “Barbie” movie to get into development, production on the sequel would still be a ways away. Robbie is in production on her “Ocean’s 11” prequel for Warner Bros. (set to release in June 2027), while Gosling just announced he’ll star in Marvel’s “Ghost Rider” movie (dated for 2028) and has to promote Disney’s “Star Wars: Starfighter” (in theaters May 28, 2027). Gerwig will also be heading out on a promo tour for her latest film, Netflix’s “Narnia,” early next year.

	That said, LuckyChap is a consistent producing partner across Warner Bros.’ slate, delivering “Wuthering Heights” earlier this year, currently in production on “Oceans” and producing the film “Nasty,” starring Rose Byrne and Jenna Ortega, for the studio’s recently launched Clockwork label. Likewise, Warner Bros. continues to engage in a close partnership with Mattel, including a Hot Wheels project in development.

title: Inside Lollapalooza’s Biggest Brand Activations: From Nütrl Vodka Seltzers to a Coca-Cola Roller Rink
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Lollapalo
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Lollapalooza’s 2026 lineup stretches far beyond the eight stages scattered throughout Chicago’s Grant Park.

	As Lorde, Charli xcx, Jennie, Tate McRae, The Smashing Pumpkins, John Summit, Olivia Dean and The xx take the stage, dozens of brands are setting up their own miniature festival destinations, offering everything from Nütrl vodka seltzers (including their just-released peach flavor) and frozen cocktails to beauty touch-ups, roller-skating, skateboarding demonstrations and a Ferris wheel overlooking the grounds. 
	

	The four-day festival kicked off Thursday and runs through Sunday, Aug. 2. Below, find a guide to the biggest sponsored activations festival-goers can visit between sets. If you can’t make it in person, the sets are streaming live on Hulu and Disney+.

	
		Nütrl	

	Nütrl Vodka Seltzer, an official sponsor of the festival, is pouring Strawberry, Pineapple, Orange and its newer Peach flavor at a dedicated on-grounds site throughout the weekend. The space also features games, photo moments and daily giveaways, giving attendees a reason to stay beyond the time it takes to pick up a can.
	
		T-Mobile Club Magenta	

	T-Mobile’s Club Magenta functions as one of the festival’s more practical pit stops where attendees can charge a dying phone, get out of the crowds for a moment and potentially leave with free merchandise.

	The carrier also has one of the most visible sponsorships on the grounds, with its name attached to one of Lollapalooza’s two main stages. Entry to the club is reserved for T-Mobile customers.
	
		Bud Light Sound Bar	

	The Bud Light Sound Bar serves as a miniature dance club inside the larger festival, with live DJs, cold beer and limited-edition merchandise drops throughout the weekend. Attendees can also enter for the chance to receive an upgrade to the festival’s VIP areas. 
	
	
		That Tito’s Thing	

	Tito’s Handmade Vodka is leaning into an old-school telephone theme with “That Tito’s Thing at Lolla Is Calling.” The space offers cocktails, midday crafts and additional surprises for attendees who “answer the call” between performances.
	
		Toyota Music Den	

	Toyota’s Music Den returns to Grant Park’s Rose Garden with its own programming and a collection of customizable festival souvenirs. Visitors can make beaded charms, collect festival bandanas and pose for fisheye portraits inside the activation.
	
		Chase Freedom Cashback Club	

	Chase cardholders can bring as many as three guests into the Chase Freedom Cashback Club, a shaded space featuring giveaways and social-media-friendly photo moments. All Chase debit and credit cardholders can also receive complimentary chargeFUZE portable battery rentals, while space inside the club is available on a first-come basis.
	
		Venmo’s Vibe Village and Stack Shop	

	Venmo is behind two experiences this year. The Venmo Stack Shop allows Cashless users to create customized festival accessories, while the larger Vibe Village combines beauty services, local shopping and food.

	The village’s Glam Suite offers festival touch-ups, while Chicago vendors sell charms and other merchandise. Its food lineup includes Gangnam Market, Matcha Cita, Candycopia, Molly’s Cupcakes, Push Sushi, Pink Mu, Kong Dog and several additional local businesses.

	PayPal and Venmo users can also receive a one-time $10 Lollapalooza Cashless credit by registering their wristbands with one of the payment services, while supplies last.
	
		Snapchat Charm Bar and Deck	

	Snapchat is giving attendees two reasons to open the app. At the Snapchat Charm Bar, fans can take a photobooth portrait and turn the image into a customized keychain decorated with their choice of charms.

	Over at Perry’s Stage, users can show the Snapchat app to enter the elevated Snapchat Deck, which offers refreshments and a less-crowded view of the electronic music stage. Visitors are encouraged to share footage from the deck through Snapchat Spotlight.
	
		Google Backstage	

	Google Shopping is turning attendees into honorary headliners at Google Backstage. Guests can pick up a mock backstage pass, virtually try on outfits, step behind a DJ booth and compete for prizes and VIP upgrades. The adjacent Google Green Room provides a place to sit down and recharge afterward.
	
	
		L.O.L. Surprise! On Tour	

	L.O.L. Surprise! is bringing its collectible dolls to Grant Park with mystery prizes, Music Festival Dolls and an installation tied to the toy brand’s collaboration with Jennie, who is among this year’s Lollapalooza headliners.
	
		Casa Bacardí	

	Located near Buckingham Fountain, the returning Casa Bacardí is one of the festival’s biggest alcohol activations. The tropical space serves rum cocktails and hosts DJs and live performers throughout the weekend, including a scheduled Walshy Fire set and performances from Puerto Rican group Las Bompleneras.
	
		Hollister Feel Good House	

	Hollister’s Feel Good House offers DJ sets, a charm bar, photo opportunities and a place to escape the summer heat. The clothing retailer has also released an official Hollister x Lollapalooza merchandise collection, available from the merch tent near Buckingham Fountain.
	
		Comfort Colors Studio	

	Comfort Colors is translating its expansive T-shirt palette into a color-focused studio. Festivalgoers can take aura photographs, pose in chromatic mirrors and return each day for collectible pins and limited airbrushed merchandise.
	
		Coca-Cola Roller Ring	

	One of the weekend’s most elaborate installations is Coca-Cola’s full roller rink. Visitors can borrow skates, circle the branded ring and pick up an ice-cold Coke before heading back to the stages.
	
		Hacienda Patrón	

	Hacienda PATRÓN brings a taste of Jalisco to Grant Park with a two-story installation serving handcrafted tequila cocktails and tacos. The 21-and-over activation also features vinyl DJ sets and unannounced surprises throughout the weekend.
	
		Neutrogena Hydro Boost Juicy Lab	

	Neutrogena’s Hydro Boost Juicy Lab gives overheated festivalgoers a skincare reset. Visitors can cool down with chilled Hydro Boost Water Gel and learn about the brand’s lightweight moisturizing products before returning to the crowds.
	
		Bubba Drip Bar	

	Drinkware brand Bubba is offering custom charm-making, laser engraving, photo opportunities and water stations. Attendees can personalize their reusable cups and bottles at the so-called Bubba Drip Bar.
	
		Liquid I.V. Flavor House	

	The Liquid I.V. Flavor House is serving hydration mixes and alcohol-free mocktails alongside giveaways and surprise DJ sets. Flavors include the new Ring Pop Cherry, Rainbow Sherbet and Raspberry Lemonade.
	
	
		The Beat Suite by Ulta Beauty	

	Ulta Beauty’s Beat Suite serves as the festival’s primary glam station, with hair and makeup refreshes, opportunities to personalize seasonal beauty trends and access to festival-exclusive products.
	
		Dunkin’ Refresherland	

	Dunkin’ is keeping the crowd caffeinated and cooled down at Refresherland, where visitors can sample the chain’s fruit-flavored Refreshers and pick up exclusive festival merchandise.
	
		Motorola Razr Wheel	

	Motorola has brought an observation wheel to Grant Park. The Razr Wheel lifts riders above the festival grounds for panoramic views and photo opportunities, while the surrounding activation offers giveaways and other interactive experiences tied to the brand’s foldable phones.
	
		Burberry Her Pop-Up	

	The Burberry Her Pop-Up translates the fragrance collection’s fruity, dessert-inspired notes into an immersive installation. Attendees can explore the perfumes through treats, scent-testing stations and photo moments.
	
		Welch’s Fusions Ultimate Remix Experience	

	Welch’s is handing out free samples of its Fusions fruit snacks, which combine multiple fruit flavors in a single bite. Visitors can also vote on a future flavor combination and participate in additional giveaways and surprises.
	
		Heinz Sauce Stop	

	Heinz once again sponsors Chow Town, Lollapalooza’s sprawling collection of Chicago food vendors. Its Sauce Stop gives attendees another branded photo opportunity before they pick up food nearby.
	
		The BeatBox Sour Spot	

	BeatBox is spotlighting its Xtreme Sour Black Cherry drink with a matching photo installation and daily merchandise giveaways. Prizes include fanny packs, graffiti-style hats, bandanas, hand fans, keychains and customized disposable cameras.
	
		Listerine Swish Tour	

	Listerine is using Lollapalooza as a stop on its limited-run Swish Tour, where visitors can try several mouthwash intensities, including a new Extra Mild option.
	
		Josh Cellars	

	At “Good Times With Josh Cellars,” wine drinkers can sample the brand’s collection, including Seaswept and the newly introduced Seaswept Sparkling. The activation is positioned as a relaxed stop for wine between afternoon sets.
	
		Aperol Day Club	

	Aperol’s Day Club brings the Italian aperitivo to Lollapalooza, inviting groups to take a break from the crowds over Aperol Spritzes.
	
	
		Jack Daniel’s Music and Karaoke Experience	

	Jack Daniel’s is offering fans their own turn behind the microphone at Cocktail North. The activation combines live karaoke with frozen cocktails and a lounge area for resting between performances.
	
		Kona Big Wave Outpost	

	Kona Big Wave has erected a branded half-pipe where professional skateboarders perform live demonstrations each day from noon to 6 p.m.
	
		Red Bull Refuel Station	

	Near Perry’s Stage, Red Bull is combining a service station, car wash and dance party aesthetic. The Refuel Station serves frozen drinks, mocktails and slushies alongside continuous DJ sets.
	
		Kidzapalooza Activations	

	Lifeway Kefir serves as the presenting sponsor of Kidzapalooza, Lollapalooza’s children’s area. Families can attend live performances, participate in interactive activities and receive free samples of Lifeway Kefir and ProBugs products.

	SmartyPants Vitamins is hosting a play-based installation centered on creativity and imagination, while Siete Foods is handing out snacks and offering crafts and a coloring station for children.
	
		Re	

	Conservation organization Re is inviting visitors to “Take a Wild Break” inside an immersive sound booth that uses audio and haptic effects to transport participants to ecosystems including Tanzania and California’s redwood forests. The space also includes giveaways and a wildlife-themed photo wall.
	
		Lolla Girl	

	Etty Lau Farrell’s Lolla Girl installation rounds out the Vibe Village programming with games, a photobooth and limited-edition merchandise. The activation is inspired by the fashion, community and colorful aesthetic that have surrounded Lollapalooza since its early years.

	Lollapalooza’s broader roster of 2026 partners also includes Allianz, Airbnb, Hulu, BMI, Uber, Uber Eats, Cutwater, Señorita, Waterloo, REVERB and Musically Fed, though the festival’s public on-site guide does not detail separate consumer activations for each of those companies. Hulu and Disney+ are serving as the official streaming destinations for select performances throughout the weekend.

title: Wild Video Shows Teen Shooter Open Fire Inside Maryland Mall, 13-Year-Old Injured
body:
Maryland Mall
                          17-Year-Old Suspect Shoots 13-Year-Old Boy ...
                          Watch The Insane Video
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 1, 2026
                            5:32 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 1, 2026
                                7:29 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A 17-year-old assailant opened fire inside a Maryland mall, hitting a 13-year-old boy in the leg as frightened shoppers ran for cover -- and the wild incident was caught on video.
      
    
            Footage of Friday night's shooting was posted on social media, and it kicks off with people calmly strolling through the Wheaton Mall in Montgomery County, MD. 
      
    
          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            The suspect, dressed all in black with a hoodie over his head, is seated at a table waiting for his chance to strike.  
      

            A bunch of teens then walk past the suspect, who suddenly jumps up and aims his handgun at them, firing several shots. Shoppers can be heard screaming as everyone scatters.
      
    
            Police said a single bullet struck the 13-year-old boy in his leg. The teen was rushed to a local hospital, where he was treated for non-life-threatening injuries. Thankfully, nobody else was injured.
      
    
            Cops said the shooter tried to make a break for it, but an armed security guard grabbed and detained him for police, who took him into custody. Charges are pending.
      
    
            Investigators did not release a motive.

                            12:15 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Shemar Moore may play a cop on TV ... but he needed the police in real life when a random woman showed up at his house ready to move in.
      
    
            Law enforcement sources tell TMZ ... cops were called to the house Friday around 3:30 p.m. after a woman arrived at his Los Angeles-area home with luggage in tow.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Our sources say the woman knocked on the door ... but instead of Shemar, we're told his significant other, Jesiree Dizon, opened the door and told the woman to leave.
      

            Jesiree later called LAPD ... who showed up and questioned the woman.
      
    
            Turns out, the woman says she wasn't there to cause harm ... our sources say she explained she'd been catfished by someone pretending to be Shemar.
      
    
            We're told she said she traveled from outside the state because the faux Shemar Moore told her he would let her live with him. Our sources say she was "easily duped."
      
    
            Law enforcement sources tell us Jesiree said she didn't want the woman arrested ... and she was released without further incident. A trespass report was taken.
      
    
            Thankfully, no need for Shemar's pals in S.W.A.T. to take down a criminal mind here ... though hopefully no one is too shaken up by the encounter.
      
    
            We've reached out to Shemar's team for more info ... so far, no word back.
